newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel falls sharply with crude.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel falls sharply with crude.

text.p: European straight-run prices fell sharply on Tuesday in line with crude futures, traders said.
A 25,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur straight-run was traded out of Scandinavia at around $105 fob a tonne to a refinery in Britain after IPE futures lost 80 cents on the barrel.
The deal reflected a sharp swing in prices from a recent high last Friday when one cargo sold at $109 fob a tonne and another moved more secretively to a distressed British refiner at $112.
One low sulphur seller said he was feeling little competition from Russian material, reflecting the continuing scarcity of good quality straight-run out of the Baltic ports.

The summer export flood from St.Petersburg has mainly been of cracked material so far. But in the Mediterranean a big Italian utility buyer said he was seeing Russian one percent straight-run on offer at floating price.
